title: Principles of a good shelter
summary: Insulation from the ground, protection from wind and water, small volume.
steps: Choose a dry, slightly raised spot, sheltered from the wind, away from dead trees and riverbeds.
Insulate yourself from the ground first: a thick layer of leaves, branches or cardboard (the ground steals more heat than the air).
Build small: just big enough to lie down, so there is less air to warm.
Face the entrance away from the prevailing wind.
Cover with a tarp, tightly packed branches or thick leaves to keep the water out.
tips: A space blanket stretched behind you, facing a fire, reflects some of the heat back to your body.
Wrapping yourself in the space blanket under your clothes or sleeping bag blocks the wind and limits heat loss.

title: Quick tarp shelter
summary: In 15 minutes with a tarp and a rope.
steps: Stretch a rope between two trees at hip height.
Lay the tarp over the rope.
Fix one side to the ground (pegs, stones) facing the wind to make a lean-to; or both sides for an A-frame tent.
Add an insulating ground mat under the shelter.

title: Sheltering in a car
summary: Stuck in snow or on the road: the car protects you, if you use it properly.
steps: Stay in the vehicle, unless a safe shelter is visible and very close.
Signal your presence: hazard lights, a coloured cloth on the aerial or window.
Run the engine only 10 minutes per hour for heat, with a window slightly open.
Regularly clear snow away from the exhaust pipe.
Cover up (blankets, clothes), move a little to keep your circulation going, drink water.
warnings: An exhaust blocked by snow = carbon monoxide inside the car, deadly within minutes.

title: Choosing where to spend the night outdoors
summary: Location mistakes you pay for at night.
steps: Set up before nightfall, one to two hours beforehand.
Avoid valley floors (cold air, damp) and exposed summits: prefer a flat spot halfway up a slope.
Never sleep in a dry riverbed or too close to water (flash floods).
Check there are no dead trees or branches overhead (“widowmakers”).
Stay near water, wood and an open area where you can be seen.
